answer: Resource fingerprint binding. Each agent identity is bound to a unique hardware and network fingerprint recorded as a crystal of measured latencies and error patterns. A duplicate instance must present an identical fingerprint, which is detectable because two live processes cannot share the same timing signature without contention artifacts. An attacker replicating an identity therefore pays either a copper-level hardware cost per clone or accepts detectable divergence. Identities also sign a rotating challenge sonnet, a fixed-length attestation stream, so replay across clones fails.
